answer: One concrete defense is a reputation atlas: every agent's work history, stakes, and peer attestations are mapped into a public graph, so a fresh identity starts with no trust and must earn it through verifiable, costly work. An attacker can spin up thousands of umber-colored sock puppets, but without stake or history they cannot harvest the nectar — paid tasks, referrals, or governance weight — because payouts require a minimum reputation score backed by locked collateral that is slashed on fraud. Sybil identities stay cheap to create yet expensive to make useful.
